QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_29

question.text: Under the CIV-scheme framework for Cat I and II AIFs, the terms of co-investment by a Manager / Sponsor / Co-investor in an investee company:

answer.text: Can be MORE favourable than the terms of the main AIF scheme's investment
Must be exactly 50% of the main AIF scheme's investment terms
SHALL NOT be MORE favourable than the terms of the main AIF scheme's investment

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the SEBI 2025 circular, terms of co-investment shall NOT be more favourable than the terms of the AIF's main investment. This prevents the manager/sponsor from cherry-picking better-economics direct exposure vs. the LP pool. The Trap: More-favourable inverts the rule. 50% is made up. 'Not regulated' ignores the circular. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests this CIV equality principle. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document co-investment terms via a 'side-by-side' comparison sheet vs. the main AIF terms — have it signed off by external IC members before each CIV deployment to pre-empt LP grievances.
